principles: Do not optimize for the sake of optimization.
Only real correctness issues justify later code changes.
Preserve logic consistency between stash groups, docs, tests, and Lattice asset roots.
drivers: Avoid whole-stash pop and mixed commits.
Make untracked stash restore mechanics explicit.
Keep planner hash change deferred unless proven.
Keep dev-memory runtime data out of commits by default.

options.name: A: Write a formal split execution decision now
pros: Makes the next implementation stories mechanically safer.
Captures Claude/Codex REQUEST CHANGES while fresh.
Does not mutate stash or code.
cons: Adds one small docs story before implementation continues.

options.name: B: Directly restore and implement stash content
cons: High risk of mixing unrelated scopes, stale NAV patch, planner hash churn, and runtime data into one commit.

options.name: C: Leave stash undocumented until later
cons: Context will decay and future agents may pop or commit the stash incorrectly.

chosen: A: Write a formal split execution decision now
rationale: Choose A because the current need is execution discipline, not code mutation. A creates a concrete, auditable path for later stories while preserving the four principles and avoiding arbitrary cleanup.

preMortem.scenario: A future agent runs git stash pop and mixes all stash content into one story.
preMortem.trigger: The plan lacks explicit restore mechanics and stop conditions.
preMortem.consequence: Runtime cleanup, Layer4 docs, planner hash behavior, and local data land together without valid evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Document bucket-specific restore commands and explicitly forbid whole-stash pop.

preMortem.scenario: NAV is updated using stale stash content.
preMortem.trigger: The agent applies the stashed NAV patch after main already added new decision entries.
preMortem.consequence: NAV count and decision links become inconsistent.
preMortem.mitigation: Document that NAV must be reconciled against current main and mechanically counted.

preMortem.scenario: Planner hash change is submitted as harmless formatting.
preMortem.trigger: The one-line hunk is kept inside a broader cleanup story.
preMortem.consequence: Forced planner run IDs change without proof or compatibility reasoning.
preMortem.mitigation: Document planner hash as deferred unless a failing repro and focused test prove correctness need.
